newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal's Lisnave to reduce capital.
newsitem.headline: Portugal's Lisnave to reduce capital.

text.p: Loss-making Portuguese ship repairer Lisnave said it would be split into two companies under a restructuring that will involve a drastic reduction in its capital.
Shares of Lisnave tumbled 43 percent in morning trade following the statement by the company in the local press.
Lisnave said it would be split into one company that will carry on ship repairing activities and another that will try to find jobs for the excess labour of the group.
The two new companies will each have a capital of 3.6 billion escudos. Lisnave presently has a capital of 35.6 billion.
The company did not say when the restructuring would be implemented.
The new ship repairer will be controlled by the Jose de Mello group and a foreign partner, the statement said.
The Portuguese state will hold a stake of no more than five percent in that company, it said.
The ship repairer, which will employ some 1,500 people, will assume Lisnave's present short term liabilities of 4.5 billion escudos.
Lisnave shares stood at 483 escudos, down 217, in volume of 564,261 at 1340 GMT.
